Change c0009. Location: 1818 Letter I; 1831 Letter I.

Context before (unchanged): But, supposing all these conjectures to be false, you cannot contest the inestimable benefit which I shall confer on all mankind to the last generation, by discovering a passage near the pole to those countries, to reach which at present so many months are requisite; or by ascertaining the secret of the magnet, which, if at all possible, can only be effected by an undertaking such as mine.

1818 text: These reflections have dispelled the agitation with which I began my letter, and I feel my heart glow with an enthusiasm which elevates me to heaven; for nothing contributes so much to tranquillize the mind as a steady purpose,—a point on which the soul may fix its intellectual eye.

1831 text: These reflections have dispelled the agitation with which I began my letter, and I feel my heart glow with an enthusiasm which elevates me to heaven; for nothing contributes so much to tranquillise the mind as a steady purpose,—a point on which the soul may fix its intellectual eye.

Diff: These reflections have dispelled the agitation with which I began my letter, and I feel my heart glow with an enthusiasm which elevates me to heaven; for nothing contributes so much to [-tranquillize-] {+tranquillise+} the mind as a steady purpose,—a point on which the soul may fix its intellectual eye.

Context after (unchanged): This expedition has been the favourite dream of my early years.

result.rationale: Only the orthography changes: 'tranquillize' becomes 'tranquillise' (-ize to -ise). The wording, meaning and sentence are otherwise identical.
